facts.raw_span: A 40-year-old man from eastern India presented with a nonhealing ulcer on the tongue present for the last 4 months
The lesion started as a small painless mass on the right lateral aspect of the tongue, which gradually grew and subsequently ulcerated
No history of trauma or tongue bite preceding the lesion
Patient denied consuming tobacco or alcohol regularly
Medical history includes well-controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus for 2 years with oral hypoglycemic agents
Single well-defined ulcer measuring 2 × 2 cm on the right lateral aspect of tongue with a clean base and irregular and elevated heaped-up margins
No underlying induration, friability, or bleeding on manipulation
Dense diffuse infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, epithelioid cells, giant cells, plasma cells, eosinophils, and neutrophils
Many histiocytes and giant cells contained intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo
Special stains (Grocott-Gomori methenamine-silver nitrate and periodic acid–Schiff) highlighted fungal forms
Fungal culture on Sabouraud dextrose agar was negative
HIV-1 and HIV-2 serologic testing were negative

concepts.why: Intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo and special stains highlighting fungal forms suggest histoplasmosis.
Dense diffuse infiltrate of lymphocytes and histiocytes with intracellular yeasts suggests candidiasis.

concepts.preferred_label: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Tongue
concepts.why: A nonhealing ulcer with irregular and elevated margins suggests squamous cell carcinoma.
Dense diffuse infiltrate of lymphocytes and histiocytes with giant cells suggests tuberculosis.
A single well-defined ulcer with a clean base and no history of trauma suggests a traumatic ulcer.
A nonhealing ulcer in a patient with well-controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus suggests a diabetic ulcer.
A nonhealing ulcer with irregular and elevated margins suggests oral leukoplakia.
A dense diffuse infiltrate of lymphocytes and histiocytes suggests oral lichen planus.

rationales.F01: Nonhealing ulcer on the tongue is a nonspecific finding
rationales.F02: Painless mass on the tongue could be a sign of malignancy
rationales.F03: No history of trauma or tongue bite makes traumatic ulcer less likely
rationales.F04: No tobacco or alcohol use decreases the likelihood of squamous cell carcinoma
rationales.F05: Well-controlled diabetes mellitus could contribute to impaired wound healing
rationales.F08: Mixed cell infiltrate is a nonspecific finding, but could be seen in infections such as histoplasmosis or candidiasis
rationales.F09: Intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo are characteristic of histoplasmosis
rationales.F10: Special stains highlighting fungal forms support the diagnosis of a fungal infection
